pairs.subject: rate-limiting
pairs.evidence: src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:40 The shared limiter is a fixed window over a process-local Map with a 5-minute reaper but no size cap, no counters, and a 429 that states retry-after but not the limit or the layer. Several techniques are realized only in part, though its distribution stance and computed Retry-After are good.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:89 Window arithmetic runs on wall-clock Date.now(), not a monotonic source. The fixed-window burst semantic and its error bound (2x across a window seam) are not stated anywhere. The count also increments on refused calls (line 99), but resetAt never moves, so it does not cause a self-renewing lockout. The durability class is stated in the header (lines 21-22).

src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:40 The map has a staleness reaper but no size cap and no LRU bound, so its cardinality is set by world-controlled keys (IPs and fp: hashes). The API also takes a caller-built key string (line 58), and the policy (limit, windowMs) is a per-call argument, not limiter state.

src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:126 Neither branch increments an admitted or refused counter, and there is no snapshot or near-limit warning. Because the limit is a call-site parameter, nothing can report a key's true limit.

src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:23 One shared module is 'the single door every rate-limited route goes through' (line 112). The distribution posture is stated explicitly as an approximation bounded by N x limit. The module does not write down a door list.

src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:127 It uses the standard 429 with a Retry-After computed from resetAt (lines 107-108, 128), spelled distinctly as code rate_limited. The refusal does not carry the rule (limit and window) or the namespace that refused, so a caller cannot pace itself. The result type is {allowed:boolean,...}, not a closed verdict.

src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:44 Good: the refusal path is O(1) and does not log. The reaper runs on a named 5-minute cadence (line 52, unref'd). But each sweep walks the whole uncapped map with no time or count bound, and it emits no metrics (pruned count, map size).

pairs.registryProposal: algorithm-selection says 'a refused attempt consumes no allowance' and asks reviewers to confirm the recording line is unreachable from the refusing branch. In a fixed window whose reset instant is set only on admission, incrementing on refusal is harmless: it cannot extend the lockout. The technique could say that the self-renewal defect needs the refused event to extend the horizon (sliding log, sub-buckets, a moving reset). Otherwise reviewers will flag harmless fixed-window increments, like the one at rate-limit.ts:99, as the shipped bug.
